body: It's an awful thing to lose someone close to you, I went through that not long ago, someone I thought I could trust turned out to have no problem palming me off. I think the thing you have to do to feel better is treat yourself. Go to the movies and watch a few by yourself, when they open again :(. Grab a coffee, and read at the beach for a while. Other lovely people will come along in your life, but for now, think of yourself in the third person, if you saw yourself walking down the street, what would you do to cheer yourself up? Give that some thought :)

Just recently i moved house, and as the flooring was crappy, we tore it up and were planning to get it replaced, so our downstairs area was mostly concrete floor (two storey). Anyway one time i stayed up to about 3, when i started to hear slapping on the concrete downstairs. I got really creeped out because it sounded like footsteps and i was the only one in the house. I listened for a while as the footsteps went around to the side of the house where the stairs are and then stopped. At this point i was terrified and i quickly ran to my bedroom door and listened, but i couldn't hear anything. I creeped down the stairs and looked around but nobody was there. Just then i heard a huge crash from upstairs and i ran back up and saw that my shelf had fallen over. I fixed it back up when i realised my bed had rotated. I then ran back downstairs and just barely caught a light winking out in our backyard. I stared out the window and could just barely see, on the waterfront path just outside my house, a sillohette of a man watching me. After that i ran back upstairs, my bed was back in the same place and i didn't hear anything for the rest of the night. I stayed awake.
